status: audit findings only; a match is a finding, not numerical or source-parity acceptance; nothing accepted; no tracker edits

records.class_level_meaning: instrument identity key of the row
records.difference_or_note: No feature header carries identity; the entity is the explicit EntityKey argument of the compute call and result metadata.

records.class_level_meaning: regular-session high of the observation row
records.difference_or_note: Same unit (currency per share) and session; the header gives a running value at a mid-session cutoff (eligible bars ending at or before the cutoff, scope marked as cutoff). Remaining difference is the sampling basis: bar-interval values versus trade-print values, and which extended-hours or auction prints are admitted, which is a caller input-contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: regular-session low of the observation row
records.difference_or_note: Same unit (currency per share) and session; the header gives a running value at a mid-session cutoff (eligible bars ending at or before the cutoff, scope marked as cutoff). Remaining difference is the sampling basis: bar-interval values versus trade-print values, and which extended-hours or auction prints are admitted, which is a caller input-contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: current-session close of the observation row
records.difference_or_note: Same unit and session. session.bar.close is the close of the last eligible interval at the cutoff; session.close.calculated_price is the last positive-volume completed-bar close. Remaining difference is the sampling basis: completed-bar close versus trade-print close, and auction-print admission as a caller input-contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: trading status of the instrument at the row
records.difference_or_note: The header is a closed-vocabulary state (active, halted, closed) selected causally from a proved supplied prefix and validity interval before the cutoff. Open contract questions: mapping of the supplied status vocabulary to the closed states, and which event the row-level status refers to relative to the cutoff.

records.class_level_meaning: path-feature completeness flag of the row
records.difference_or_note: Availability flags are not feature headers. Readiness of the paired numeric header is reported as per-output status and quality in the result, not as a value; whether such a flag is derived from that readiness or supplied is a contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: serialized volume-anomaly summary blob
records.difference_or_note: No header exists; a structured blob is not a scalar feature value.

records.class_level_meaning: event time of the latest applied observation
records.difference_or_note: No header echoes an event time. session.clock.* are functions of the supplied evaluation cutoff and calendar, not of the latest observation.

records.class_level_meaning: latest price at the evaluation time
records.difference_or_note: session.bar.close is the close of the last eligible interval at the cutoff, so it tracks the latest regular-session price at bar granularity. Open contract questions: bar-close versus trade-print basis and whether extended-hours prints are in scope; no trade-print last-price header exists.

records.class_level_meaning: running regular-session high at the evaluation cutoff
records.difference_or_note: Same unit (currency per share) and session; the header gives a running value at a mid-session cutoff (eligible bars ending at or before the cutoff, scope marked as cutoff). Remaining difference is the sampling basis: bar-interval values versus trade-print values, and which extended-hours or auction prints are admitted, which is a caller input-contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: running regular-session low at the evaluation cutoff
records.difference_or_note: Same unit (currency per share) and session; the header gives a running value at a mid-session cutoff (eligible bars ending at or before the cutoff, scope marked as cutoff). Remaining difference is the sampling basis: bar-interval values versus trade-print values, and which extended-hours or auction prints are admitted, which is a caller input-contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: change of the current price versus the prior regular close
records.difference_or_note: session.price.close_close_return (fraction, C/P-1 with a compatible prior close P) is the regular-session carrier; session.extended.prior_close_return covers premarket and postmarket phases. Remaining differences: price basis (bar close versus latest print), phase scope, and unit (fraction versus percent) as a presentation conversion. Ledger note: prior_close_return exists only as session.extended.prior_close_return; calendar.period.* has none.

records.class_level_meaning: prior-close availability flag
records.difference_or_note: Availability flags are not feature headers. Readiness of the paired numeric header is reported as per-output status and quality in the result, not as a value; whether such a flag is derived from that readiness or supplied is a contract item.

records.class_level_meaning: supplied sector classification label
records.difference_or_note: The header returns the causal active membership text for the selected membership kind (sector, industry or universe), one producer configuration per kind. The gate state and reason headers carry availability.

records.class_level_meaning: supplied industry classification label
records.difference_or_note: The header returns the causal active membership text for the selected membership kind (sector, industry or universe), one producer configuration per kind. The gate state and reason headers carry availability.

records.class_level_meaning: as-of date identity of the relative value
records.difference_or_note: No header or metadata echo of a relative-value as-of date exists; the concept belongs to relative-value producers, which are not EF1 headers on main.

records.class_level_meaning: premarket high
records.difference_or_note: The header is the extremum of supplied completed interval highs inside the supplied premarket phase prefix. Caller-contract items: which print basis (interval bars or trade prints) and which admission rule the contract must state; phase bounds are supplied calendar segments in the header.

records.class_level_meaning: premarket low
records.difference_or_note: The header is the extremum of supplied completed interval lows inside the supplied premarket phase prefix. Caller-contract items: which print basis (interval bars or trade prints) and which admission rule the contract must state; phase bounds are supplied calendar segments in the header.

records.class_level_meaning: price of the first regular-session trade
records.difference_or_note: Same meaning: first eligible regular-session trade price, currency per share. The delivery ledger attributes this producer to #506, which bears on the D8 owner question.

records.class_level_meaning: opening gap of the regular open versus the prior close
records.difference_or_note: The header is the fraction (O-P)/P with O the first selected regular sample (trade sampling) and P the supplied prior close. Caller-contract items: unit (fraction versus a percent presentation) and behaviour when the prior close is absent (header: null with reasons).

records.class_level_meaning: fraction of the opening gap filled by the latest price
records.difference_or_note: Same clamped fill ratio on the final selected observation, as a fraction. Caller-contract items: unit (fraction versus a percent presentation), which prints count as the latest price (header: final selected observation inside the regular path scope), and zero-gap or absent-input behaviour (header: null with reasons).

records.class_level_meaning: prior-day high
records.difference_or_note: history.prior_high is the prior-only rolling high over N complete prior governed slots, excluding the target; too few slots gives insufficient history rather than a smaller window. Alternative carrier: session.daily_observations.high with selector last_observations (N of 1 to 252 admitted observations, not a session count; a short history yields a smaller window or a null with insufficient-history status per _daily_context.py and _daily.py), prior-only. Window rule (observation count versus calendar span), admission and minimum history are caller-contract items.

Inclusion of the target and minimum history are caller-contract items.

Treatment of an empty prior period is a caller-contract item.

records.difference_or_note: Daily history is an input role of the period and daily-observation producers; no header outputs history. Length, adjustment and completed-only versus current-inclusive profile are not fixed by any merged header.

records.class_level_meaning: count of history bars excluded by quality screening
records.difference_or_note: session.daily_observations.selected_observed_count counts raw-admitted selected observations, not excluded ones, and no other EF1 header carries an exclusion count.

records.class_level_meaning: close of the last completed session of the reference history
records.difference_or_note: Daily observations expose open, high, low and a count but no close. session.close.calculated_price is the close of the target session, a different time position.

records.class_level_meaning: corporate-action suspicion flag from the reference history
